ideas.ablation_behavior_off: Set b_i=0 and alpha=0 in the coupled assignment; retain identical negative curvature, level sizes, tail margin, and train-only collision rank protocol (rank key falls back to item id). This tests whether behaviour contributes.

ideas.behavior_computation: train_successor_signal takes only the Stage 2 training split and item count; count adjacent i->j edges, derive outdegree_i=sum_j C[i,j], return standardized log1p(outdegree_i) (zero for unobserved items). No validation/test sequences or frequencies are passed.
ideas.behavior_signal: Per-item training-only outgoing transition popularity b_i, as returned by train_successor_signal(train_split).
ideas.cost_estimate: Precompute signal in O(number of train transitions), O(number of items) memory. Per assignment adds one scalar-code bias and level-3 Poincare distances, O(B*K3) scalar work beyond baseline geometry. At frozen scale, 24 full-item steps/epoch means 589,344 item assignments/epoch and 1,768,032,000 over 3000 epochs; added work is 589,344*K3 scalar bias operations per epoch (K3=256: about 151M), plus small segment reductions for occupied (z1,z2) groups. ideas.coupling_equation: z3_i=argmin_k[d_P(expmap0(r_i,c3),expmap0(e_3k,c3);c3)-alpha*tanh(b_i)h_k]; therefore behaviour and curved distance jointly determine the three-token prefix whose collision group is ranked.
ideas.coupling_path: train-only b_i modulates a code-specific bias inside the level-3 Poincare-distance argmin; changing b_i changes the selected anchor, and replacing d_P changes the same argmin. The ensuing (z1,z2,z3) groups determine the ranked extension token.

On canonical 52,855-pair / ten-fixed-negative evaluation predict L1 Hard ER stays near baseline or slightly improves (not the optimization target); gold-prefix survival at depth 1 is near coarse-arm 0.989, depth 2 roughly >=0.34, depth 3 and 4 rise over resample's .091/.088 because decisive T3/T4 preserve continuation. ideas.hyperbolic_location: Level-3 hard code assignment during all 3000 Stage 2 epochs; used again only in the assignment logits, not for post-hoc relabeling.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Poincare distance d_P at fixed negative curvature -c3 (c3=0.5), with expmap0 of residuals and code anchors.
ideas.key_change: Let level 1 retain 32 effective groups, level 2 retain the baseline 256 codes, and perform a behaviour-conditioned Poincare nearest-code assignment at level 3. For items sharing (z1,z2,z3), sort by smoothed training successor popularity and assign deterministic ranks 0..9 (bucket larger groups into ten rank bins); append that rank as token 4.
ideas.leakage_boundary: The function receives only train split; the tensor is fixed before Stage 2 fitting. Validation/test interactions, metrics, and item counts cannot enter b_i, assignment, tail loss, or collision ordering. Stage 3 test is evaluation only.
ideas.motivation: Make the third code carry a train-only successor-community choice and make collisions under the first three codes resolve in a reproducible, recommendation-relevant order rather than an arbitrary fourth-token choice.
ideas.novelty: Unlike existing successor-geodesic coarse assignment or tangent successor residuals, use one scalar train-only successor statistic to condition the actual Poincare assignment at level 3, then use that same statistic only to order collisions after the three-token prefix is frozen. The extension is explicitly not a fourth quantizer level and is excluded from every prefix-consistency loss.

rebuttal.remaining: The scalar cannot represent successor identity/community, and this mechanism may amount only to popularity-dependent code bias; conditional recommendation value of the tail ranking remains unestablished until the stated held-out comparison succeeds.
rebuttal.unchanged: Keep train-only standardized log1p(outdegree) as b_i, the existing code-specific h_k bias in level-3 Poincare assignment, the existing deterministic within-triple outdegree rank for z4, and the fixed-width representation.
rebuttal.why: This corrects the interpretation and makes conditional relevance an explicit falsifiable requirement without changing the assignment mechanism or adding a score; the equal-outdegree/disjoint-successor counterexample is accepted as showing that b_i cannot distinguish those communities.

risks: A global outgoing-popularity scalar may not distinguish competing interests; small collision groups produce ties; balance penalty can create artificial child occupancy and hurt semantic fit; overly strong alpha can reorder items by popularity rather than transitions.
ideas.safeguards: Clamp std to 1e-6, tanh behaviour and code biases, clamp Poincare norms to (1-1e-5)/sqrt(c3), compute artanh arguments in [-1+1e-6,1-1e-6], normalize counts only among occupied children, skip p with fewer than two occupied children, use fixed item-ID ties, log assignment histograms and NaN/Inf checks. Checker can substitute real b, its mean (constant behavior), and zeros through the same function output pathway.
ideas.spec_equations: C_ij=count_train(i->j); b_i=(log(1+sum_j C_ij)-mean_train)/max(std_train,1e-6). d_ik=d_P(exp_0(r_i),exp_0(e_k);c3)-alpha*tanh(b_i)h_k; z3_i=argmin_k d_ik. L=L_RQVAE+lambda_tail sum_p relu(max_c n_pc-min_c n_pc-2)^2, p=(z1,z2), counts over items and z3 only. After fitting, for each exact triple group sort (-outdegree_i,item_id), assign z4=min(9,floor(10*rank/m)). Four-token fixed width; no fourth-level continuation penalty.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Input item embeddings/residuals, existing z1/z2 assignments, level-3 codebook, train split, item IDs; output level-3 hard assignments, RQ-VAE plus tail loss, and deterministic four-token SID. train_successor_signal(train_split) returns shape [24556] float tensor.

specification.text: Construct b_i with train_successor_signal(train_split): count each adjacent training-only transition i->j, compute s_i=sum_j C[i,j]/(1+sum_j C[i,j]), then standardize log1p(outdegree_i) across items to mean zero/unit variance (zero for absent items); return an item-indexed float tensor. On level 3 compute q_i=expmap0(r_i,c3), where r_i is the current Euclidean residual; candidate anchors a_k=expmap0(e_3k,c3). Set d_ik=d_P(q_i,a_k;c3) - alpha*tanh(b_i)*h_k, where h_k is a learned scalar per code constrained to [-1,1], then choose argmin_k d_ik. This gives a genuine behaviour-conditioned curved assignment. After training, group by exactly z1,z2,z3; sort each group by (-log1p(outdegree_i), item_id) and set z4=min(9,floor(10*rank/group_size)); use deterministic item_id tie break. No penalty averages over z4. Tail balance is enforced on the training tensors: for each parent p=(z1,z2), let n_pc be number of training items assigned to child c=z3; minimize L_tail=sum_p max(0, max_c n_pc - (min_c n_pc + 2))^2 after restricting to occupied children (margin=2 counts; intended inequality max_c n_pc <= min_c n_pc+2). This is measured from the same z1,z2,z3 assignment tensors used by training, with stop-gradient counts and a straight-through assignment gradient to level-3 logits.

specification.text: Define train_successor_signal(train_split) returning two per-item tensors: b_i=outgoing transition entropy normalized to [0,1] and vector sparse neighbor rows P_i. Count adjacent transitions per training sequence; P_ij=(C_ij+1e-3)/(outdegree_i+1e-3*|N_i|) over observed outgoing neighbors. Set c_i=clip(c_min+(c_max-c_min)*b_i, c_min,c_max), with c_min=.25,c_max=1.0; hence concentrated successor profiles get lower curvature. Use d_P(exp_0(r_i,c_i), exp_0(e_k,c_i);c_i) for level-3 assignment. For batch item pairs i,j sharing the current (z1,z2) parent, define overlap o_ij=sum_k min(P_ik,P_jk); sample a positive if o_ij>=.25 and a negative if o_ij<=.05. Let v_i=log_0(exp_0(r_i,c_i),c_i), a differentiable tangent representative of the current third-level residual. L_pref=sum_(+,−) relu(m+d_P(v_i,v_j;cbar)-d_P(v_i,v_−;cbar)) with cbar=sqrt(c_i*c_j), computed only over z1,z2,z3 representations (never z4). Also tail-balance counts on the same z1,z2,z3 assignment tensors enforce max_c n_pc <= min_c n_pc+2 for occupied children, via squared hinge. For each g=(q1,q2), m_g=Frechet_L({x_i^3:i in g}), p_g=normalize_L(sum_i(1+b_i)mu^3_{q3(i)}); Lclose=mean_g d_L(m_g,p_g)^2. Sort each exact (q1,q2,q3) item group by (-n_i,item_id), set q4=rank mod 32. Here n_i=sum_j C_ij. No q4 member enters Lclose or the prefix representative calculation.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs are Stage-2 item vectors/residuals, training interaction split, four codebooks and fixed SID width. Output is four integer tokens per item plus RQ-VAE parameters and logged diagnostics. Behaviour function input is train split and item count; output is float32 [N].

specification.text: Let b_i be the normalized successor entropy below. At each residual quantization level, map item residual y_i to Lorentz point x_i=exp^L_o([s*y_i, a*(b_i-mean(b))]), with curvature -c, c=1 and clipped a; assign to code c_k minimizing d_L(x_i,mu_k)^2. For batch items sharing hard prefix (q1,q2), let m_g be the Lorentz Frechet mean (2 fixed Karcher steps) of their third-level targets x_i and let p_g be the normalized behaviour-weighted mean of their third-level prototypes; Lclose=mean_g d_L(m_g,p_g)^2, only for levels 1-3. Optimize reconstruction + commitment + 0.1 Lclose. For every exact three-code collision group G, sort items by descending train-only successor count n_i (ties ascending item ID); assign fourth token rank modulo M=32, with deterministic fixed-width token encoding; do not train or penalize level 4 as part of Lclose.

ideas.title: Branch-conditioned Lorentz prefix closure with popularity-ordered collision tails

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: Set p_ij to a uniform distribution over items for each source (and disable popularity ordering, using item-ID tie-break); retain all curved operators, closure, and matched training. Predict loss of branch-directed residual signal and lower T3/depth-3 survival and T4 predictability than both-on.
ideas.ablation_both_on: Use actual train successor profiles, curved tangent residual transport at curvature -1, three-token-prefix closure only, and train-popularity rank extension. Keep only if both top-1 tail positions and depths 3-4 improve over both ablations and frozen Stage3 test_R@10 >0.065.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: Use tangent identity coordinates, ordinary vector subtraction and squared Euclidean third-code distance; keep the exact observed C_ij/p_ij, popularity ordering, closure terms, and parameter budget. This is a matched Euclidean assignment, not removal of behaviour. Predict weaker T3 conditional separation and lower depth-3/4 survival than both-on; compare ER and Stage3 equally.
ideas.behavior_computation: Named function successor_profile_by_item(train_split,n_items) returns (CSR C[N,N], b[N], n[N]) from consecutive item pairs in training sequences only; p_ij=C_ij/(sum_j C_ij+1e-12), b_i normalized entropy, n_i=sum_j C_ij. Cache CSR rows and sample at most 16 nonzero successors with probabilities renormalized for minibatch computation.
ideas.behavior_signal: Directed train successor probability row p_ij plus outgoing count n_i; normalized row entropy b_i.
ideas.cost_estimate: 24 updates/epoch for 3000 epochs, four cards; sparse successor rows cached and at most 16 sampled outgoing edges per item/step. Extra log/exp maps and distance only for third code, O(batch*(16+d*256)) with code distances already required; estimated 3-6% wall time. One-time sort O(N log N); no added full pairwise graph tensor.
ideas.coupling_equation: x_i^3=exp^L_{mu_{q1,q2}}(clip(z_i-eta*sum_j p_ij log^L_{mu_{q1,q2}}(mu^3_{q3(j)}),R)); q3(i)=argmin_k d_L(x_i^3,mu_k^3)^2, where p_ij is the named train successor signal and log/exp/d_L are curvature -1 operators.
ideas.coupling_path: C_ij determines p_ij and the successor-code barycentre v_i; v_i is subtracted from the tangent residual before exp^L and geodesic argmin chooses q3. Thus behaviour changes the input point and geometry changes the selected q3; disabling either breaks that same path.

evidence_revision.evidence_note: Positive row scalar leaves every arg-min unchanged: True. Codeword-dependent weight moved 0 top-1 assignments.

ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: The transport subtracts the item's likely-successor branch direction from its third residual, making q3 a stable context/branch discriminator instead of a fresh arbitrary code choice; popularity rank makes T4 predictable. Require both-on T3 accuracy and depth-3/4 survival to exceed controls and Stage3 test_R@10 >0.065. L1 Hard ER on canonical 52,855 pairs/ten fixed negatives is expected unchanged or modestly worse; a large ER gain with no survival/Recall gain is not success.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: Third residual formation and level-3 code selection within Stage 2, plus a level-1-to-3 prefix-only continuation regularizer; no fourth-level quantization/penalty.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Lorentz log map at the (q1,q2) prefix representative, tangent-vector subtraction, exp map, and Lorentz geodesic nearest-code assignment, curvature -1.
ideas.key_change: At level 3, transport the item's Euclidean residual into the tangent space at the current Lorentz prefix representative, subtract a bounded successor-distribution barycentre direction, then exp-map and choose the nearest third-level code by Lorentz distance. Keep levels 1-2 normal RQ and use the same three-prefix-only continuation closure and popularity-ranked deterministic extension.
ideas.leakage_boundary: The profile function accepts only the training split; it is called once before Stage 2. Successor targets and popularity ranks are built from train interactions only. No validation or test interaction, metric, or sequence is read during SID learning, ordering, or hyperparameter choice.
ideas.motivation: A coarse first code can preserve many gold prefixes yet leave the third decision effectively 256-way; the third residual should encode which training successor branch an item's two-token context supports, and the collision extension should exploit a small deterministic popularity order.
ideas.novelty: The behaviour signal is not used as a pairwise attraction or suffix: it selects a per-item tangent transport direction before curved third-level quantization. The direction is estimated from the training successor distribution's codebook barycentre, so it changes the actual residual presented to the third-level hyperbolic quantizer. The fourth token is independently prescribed as a train-popularity rank within exact first-three collisions.
ideas.observables: Log canonical L1 Hard ER (52,855 pairs, ten fixed negatives), gold-prefix survival at each depth, teacher-forced top-1 T3/T4 and T4 NLL/alphabet, and frozen Stage3 test_R@10. Expected L1 ER roughly unchanged/slight increase; depth 1-2 neutral, depth 3-4 higher; T3 top-1 moves from the 0.34 region toward 0.7 and T4 toward 0.977; Stage3 should cross 0.065 if the gains translate to beam coverage.
risks: Successor-target assignments are nonstationary and may oscillate; high-outdegree rows need sampling; transport can erase useful content residual; groups with >32 items alias in q4; train successor labels may be sparse for cold items.
ideas.safeguards: Curvature fixed at -1; use stable Lorentz exp/log formulas with inner-product clamps and valid-sheet projection; cap successor row sampling to 16 with renormalized p; define empty rows v_i=0 and b_i=0; detach q3 targets in v_i to prevent moving-target gradient loops; clip tangent norm to R and gradient norm; clamp Frechet weights and skip singleton groups; deterministic item-ID ties and modulo-32 extension; preserve separate level-4 generation and exclude it from all prefix losses.
ideas.spec_equations: p_ij=C_ij/(n_i+eps); b_i=H(p_i)/log(max(2,nnz(C_i))). z_i=log^L_{mu_{q1,q2}}(exp^L_o(s*y_i)); v_i=sum_j p_ij log^L_{mu_{q1,q2}}(mu^3_{q3(j)}), with target codes detached; x_i^3=exp^L_{mu_{q1,q2}}(clip(z_i-eta*v_i,R)); q3=argmin_k d_L(x_i^3,mu^3_k)^2. For g=(q1,q2), m_g=Frechet_L({mu^3_{q3(i)}:i in g}, weights 1+b_i); Lclose=mean_{i} d_L(mu^3_{q3(i)},m_g)^2, where g and members use only first three positions, never q4. q4 ranks members of each exact (q1,q2,q3) collision by (-n_i,item_id) mod 32.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs are frozen item vectors, Stage-2 train split, current first-two codes and Lorentz representatives, third codebook, and RQ-VAE optimizer state. Outputs are third-code assignments/updates and four-token SIDs; the behavior function returns sparse successor profiles, entropy, and counts.

specification.text: Learn/initialize Lorentz prototypes mu_k^3 for third code. For each item, compute z_i=log^L_{mu_{q1,q2}}(exp^L_o(s*y_i)); compute v_i=sum_j p_ij log^L_{mu_{q1,q2}}(mu^3_{q3(j)}) where successor target j's current third code is detached and p_ij=C_ij/(sum_j C_ij+eps). Then r_i=clip_norm(z_i-eta*stopgrad(v_i),R), x_i^3=exp^L_{mu_{q1,q2}}(r_i), q3=argmin_k d_L(x_i^3,mu_k^3)^2. Use Lclose over only first-three prefix representatives: within each hard (q1,q2), penalize squared Lorentz distance between each item's third representative and the group's behaviour-weighted Frechet mean, with weight (1+b_i). Tail q4 sorts exact three-token collision members by descending n_i, then item ID, assigning rank mod 32.

ideas.title: Behaviour-directed curved residual transport for decisive third codes

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: Set b_i=mean(b) and p_i=mean(p) for every item, retaining the same Lorentz implementation, continuation margin, K, and compute. This removes item-conditioned behavior from curvature and extension ordering; expect lower T3/T4 and prefix survival than both-on.
ideas.ablation_both_on: Use actual b_i-conditioned Lorentz map/distance and actual p_i popularity ordering, with the three-level-only continuation margin; evaluate all listed observables and fixed Stage 3 protocol.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: Replace exp_o^k and d_L,k in assignment and continuation penalty with matched Euclidean z3 and squared Euclidean distance, retaining actual b_i-dependent scale in the assignment score only as a matched scalar temperature is not allowed: instead map k_i to a Euclidean anisotropic metric M_i=diag(exp(k_i),exp(-k_i),1...) and use (z-c)^T M_i(z-c), so behavior remains coupled but curvature is absent. This isolates geometry; expect worse T3/prefix survival than both-on.
ideas.behavior_computation: make_train_behavior(train_split) returns tensors b[N] and p[N]. Count directed adjacent item pairs only inside each user's training sequence; b_i=-sum_j P(j|i)log(P(j|i)+eps)/log(max(2,degree_i)); p_i=log(1+sum_j count(i,j)). No validation/test sequences are read.
ideas.behavior_signal: Per-item normalized entropy of the directed training-only next-item distribution, plus the same training-only outgoing count for extension ordering.
ideas.cost_estimate: Behavior statistics are one preprocessing pass over train transitions, O(E_train); curvature and distance require O(N*256) level-3 code comparisons per assignment step and one sampled prefix triplet per transition minibatch. Relative to baseline: modest (about one extra level-3 distance evaluation and sampled penalty; expected 5-15% step time, measure). Frozen scale: 24 steps/epoch * 3000 = 72,000 steps; add at most 72,000 level-3 batched distance calls and 72,000 sampled triplet-penalty calls, each on the existing minibatch (no all-pairs matrix); 4 cards data-parallel.
ideas.coupling_path: Training outgoing entropy b_i sets k_i, which changes exp_o and Lorentz distances to level-3 codewords, changing the chosen third code; that changed code defines q123 for the continuation margin. Popularity p_i separately determines only deterministic fourth-token order after the prefix is frozen.

evidence_revision.answers: the probe found positive row-scalar weighting leaves every arg-min unchanged, and codeword-dependent weighting moved 0 top-1 assignments
evidence_revision.evidence_note: Positive row scalar: arg-min unchanged, measured True. Codeword-dependent weight: 0 top-1 assignments moved. No evidence supplied for a benefit from the proposed curvature or prefix coupling (UNKNOWN).
evidence_revision.revision: The proposal makes no evidence-supported claim that per-item curvature can move the level-3 arg-min assignment; it retains that operation only as an unvalidated hypothesis, with no claimed routing benefit
evidence_revision.withdrawn: The claim that branching-entropy-conditioned curvature makes third codes more branch-informative by changing assignments

ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: High-branching items benefit from greater negative curvature's hierarchy separation, making third codes more branch-informative; same-prefix continuation margin makes T3 predictable, and popularity ranks make T4 nearly deterministic. Keep only if both-on improves gold-prefix survival at depths 3 and 4 and teacher-forced T3/T4 accuracy, with Stage 3 test_R@10 >0.065; report L1 Hard ER on the canonical 52,855 pairs and ten fixed negatives as a guard against pathological collapse.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: Level-3 code assignment and the level-3 three-token-prefix continuation penalty during Stage 2 quantizer training.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Lorentz-model distance d_L,k with trainable/fixed negative curvature -k, and Lorentz exponential map exp_o^k; k is bounded to [0.05,2.0].
ideas.key_change: Compute normalized branching entropy per item from training transitions, convert it to a bounded item curvature, and assign level-3 residuals by Lorentz distance under that curvature. Optimize the three-token representatives (levels 1-3 only) with a margin continuation penalty; afterward order items sharing a three-token prefix by training successor popularity to allocate the small fourth-token extension alphabet.
ideas.leakage_boundary: The function accepts only the train split and returns item-indexed tensors; SID fitting, curvature, penalty sampling, and extension ordering consume only those tensors and training embeddings. Freeze resulting SID mapping before Stage 3 evaluation; validation/test interactions are inaccessible to construction.
ideas.motivation: Items reached through many distinct next-item contexts need a stable, coarse first token, while the third token should resolve the remaining ambiguity using the actual train-only successor branch.
ideas.novelty: Instead of adding successor distance as an independent loss or applying it to a residual, use per-item successor-branch entropy to set the curvature of a single Lorentz nearest-code assignment at level 3; the selected level-3 code is then constrained through its three-token prefix representative. Keep collision extension as a separate deterministic post-assignment operation.
ideas.observables: Compare L1 Hard ER on the fixed canonical 52,855-pair/10-negative set; gold-prefix survival depths 1,2,3,4; teacher-forced top-1 T3 and T4; Stage 3 test_R@10. Predicted T3 rises materially above the measured 0.338 coarse-geodesic arm, T4 approaches the resample 0.977, depth-3/4 survival and test recall rise, while L1 ER may change but should not exhibit total collapse. Include explicit behavior-off, Euclidean geometry-off, and both-on runs.
risks: Curvature heterogeneity may destabilize shared codebooks; entropy is noisy for rare items; sampled negatives may produce false continuation structure; a 32-slot extension bucket can be exceeded; a coarse L1 gain can be lost to code usage imbalance. ER may rise or fall, so it is diagnostic, not the selection rule.
ideas.safeguards: Clamp probabilities before log; define entropy as zero for outdegree<2; bound k away from zero and cap Lorentz coordinates/norm before exp map; stable acosh(max(1+eps, Lorentz inner product)); normalize tangent vectors; gradient-clip; deterministic item-id tie-break; extension code count fixed and explicitly fail/log overflow rather than silently reusing rank; sample non-successor only among train items; assert continuation tensors are q123 only.
ideas.spec_equations: For each batch: compute u_i=exp_o^{k_i}(z3_i); a_i=argmin_c d_L,k_i(u_i,c)^2; q123_i=compose(q1_i,q2_i,c[a_i]); sample transition (i,j) and matched-prefix non-successor n; Lcont=relu(m+d_L,k0(q123_i,q123_j)-d_L,k0(q123_i,q123_n)); update model/codebooks on L_RQVAE+lambda Lcont. After training, per prefix sort by (-p_i,item_id), set t4=floor(rank/32) clipped to available extension codes; output fixed four-token SID. Prefix quantities never include t4.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs: train split sequences, item embeddings, four-level RQ-VAE codebooks, train transitions, hyperparameters k0/alpha/kmin/kmax/lambda/m and K=32. Outputs: trained codebooks, item SID tensor [N,4], b[N], p[N], and logged L1 ER/prefix survival/T3-T4 accuracies. The behavior function must return real, mean-filled, and zero-filled controls for independent coupling checks.

specification.text: Let b_i be normalized outgoing-successor entropy and p_i be log(1+training successor count), both computed by make_train_behavior(train_split). For level 3 use k_i=clip(k0*exp(alpha*(b_i-mean(b))), kmin,kmax), kmin,kmax>0. Map level-3 residual z_i to Lorentz space with exp_o^{k_i}; choose c*=argmin_c d_L,k_i(exp_o^{k_i}(z_i),c)^2. The prefix penalty uses only representative vectors q123 (composed from levels 1,2,3): for each training transition i->j with same first two assigned codes, penalize max(0,m+d_L(q123_i,q123_j) - d_L(q123_i,q123_n)), where n is a sampled non-successor with same first-two prefix. Train the four-level RQ-VAE reconstruction/commitment objective plus lambda times this penalty. Within each exact first-three-code bucket, sort by (-p_i,item_id), assign extension ranks in fixed chunks of size K=32 (fourth token 0..31); never include level 4 in prefix-penalty averages.

ideas.title: Branch-conditioned Lorentz prefix routing with a decisive third code

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: Set s_i to its train-item mean, replace A with uniform outgoing probabilities over train items, and use uniform r_i; keep Lorentz costs, Sinkhorn, prefix balance structure, and extension algorithm (mean popularity ties resolved by item ID). Expect reduced T3/T4, survival, and recall if behavior is useful.
ideas.ablation_both_on: Use train-derived s_i/A in row masses and prefix successor mass, Lorentz C_ic and Lorentz prefix hinge, then deterministic popularity extension; evaluate under frozen Stage 3 protocol.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: Use Euclidean C_ic=||z3_i-v_c||^2 and Euclidean prefix representative distances in the hinge, with the exact same actual s_i/A, row masses, capacities, temperature, and Sinkhorn iterations. This is a matched Euclidean assignment preserving behavior; expect worse T3 and depth-3/4 survival than both-on if curvature adds value.
ideas.behavior_computation: make_train_behavior(train_split) returns sparse A[N,N] and s[N]. Extract consecutive (item_t,item_t+1) pairs within each user's train sequence, count edges, row-normalize nonempty rows, and set s_i=log(1+incoming count). Use no non-training split.
ideas.behavior_signal: Training-only incoming popularity mass s_i and directed row-normalized item transition graph A_ij.
ideas.cost_estimate: Sparse transition aggregation is O(E_train); each Sinkhorn minibatch is O(B*256*I) for I=8-12 iterations, plus Lorentz costs O(B*256), and prefix balance is O(number of occupied prefixes squared within matched first-two groups), implement with top sibling pairs to bound it. At frozen scale, 72,000 optimizer steps; with B equal to baseline minibatch, 8-12 small Sinkhorn iterations per step; expect roughly 10-25% Stage 2 wall-clock overhead, record actual step time. No full 24,556^2 matrix or extra epoch.
ideas.coupling_path: s_i sets transport row mass, A_ij contributes prefix successor mass, and Lorentz C_ic determines where that weighted mass is transported; T changes level-3 hard codes and therefore q123 prefix membership, which changes the balance hinge and emitted SIDs.

evidence_revision.evidence_note: Positive row scalar left every arg-min unchanged (True); codeword-dependent weight moved False of the top-1; no other measured numbers provided
evidence_revision.revision: The proposal no longer claims that behavior-derived positive row demand weights move item-to-code arg-min assignments; the evidence does not establish that behavior changes the constrained assignment itself
evidence_revision.withdrawn: The claim that behavior weighting changes assignments and prevents transition-important items from being stranded in level-3 codes

ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: Behavior-weighted capacity prevents transition-important items from being stranded in overloaded level-3 codes, while the curved cost assigns semantically and behaviorally compatible residuals. T3 top-1 should rise toward 0.7, the level-3 prefix margin should increase depth-3/4 survival, and popularity-ranked extension should make T4 highly accurate with a small alphabet. Worth keeping only if fixed-protocol Stage 3 test_R@10 exceeds 0.065 and both-on wins over the two matched ablations; L1 Hard ER is reported on canonical 52,855 pairs with ten fixed negatives to ensure the coarse level did not merely collapse.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: Cost matrix for level-3 soft/hard code assignment during Stage 2; same assignment flows into three-token prefix representatives and behavior successor-mass balancing.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Lorentz exponential map and Lorentz geodesic distance with fixed negative curvature -k (k=1 initially); no Euclidean distance in both-on transport.
ideas.key_change: At level 3, use a small entropic transport solve over item-to-code assignments with behavior-derived item demand and geodesic item-to-code cost. Add a three-token-prefix balance hinge that explicitly pushes every overloaded prefix's represented successor mass to a sibling prefix by a margin; then sort members of each final three-token prefix by training successor popularity for extension tokens.
ideas.leakage_boundary: The named function's sole input is train_split; its outputs are persisted with the Stage 2 run and are the only interaction-derived tensors used in transport, prefix balance, and extension ranking. Validation/test data never enter preprocessing, assignment, tuning, or SID ordering.
ideas.motivation: A transition's next item should receive a third code that is both useful for reconstructing item semantics and geometrically aligned with its training successor context; the observed coarse-first-level solution otherwise leaves level 3 too weak to disambiguate continuation.
ideas.novelty: Couple behavior and geometry in a minibatch transport assignment: training transition counts define row demand weights and Lorentz geodesic costs jointly determine which level-3 residual codes receive items. This is not a successor-geodesic auxiliary loss; behavior changes the constrained assignment itself. The fourth token remains deterministic popularity-ranked extension, not a fourth interchangeable quantizer level.
ideas.observables: Report canonical L1 Hard ER (52,855 pairs, same ten fixed negatives), gold-prefix survival at each depth 1-4, teacher-forced top-1 T3/T4, and Stage 3 test_R@10. Predicted depth-3 survival and T3 increase versus the measured coarse-geodesic arm; depth-4 survival/T4 increase versus it through compact popularity-ranked extension; target recall >0.065. L1 ER could rise modestly from balancing but not collapse. Compare behavior-off, Euclidean geometry-off, and both-on.
risks: Sinkhorn may be too costly or underflow with sharply varying costs; weighted capacities can overconcentrate high-degree items; minibatch transport may not match global code capacities; successor mass is sparse for rare items; the balance hinge could trade away reconstruction quality. Fixed extension capacity may overflow dense prefixes.
ideas.safeguards: Log-domain Sinkhorn; clamp costs and logits; ensure positive marginals and renormalize r/h; use deterministic bounded iterations; for empty outgoing rows set A row zero; define prefix balance only for occupied siblings and cap pair sampling; stop gradients through discrete prefix membership but keep soft transport gradients; report row/column marginal error; stable Lorentz acosh clamp and bounded coordinates; deterministic tie-break by item ID; log extension overflow explicitly; assert all prefix balance terms reference exactly levels 1-3.
ideas.spec_equations: Form C_ic from level-3 residual and Lorentz codeword. r_i=(1+gamma*s_i)/sum_i(1+gamma*s_i); h_c=1/256. Run fixed-I log-domain Sinkhorn on K_ic=-C_ic/tau with marginals r,h; use soft T in quantizer gradients, hard argmax for four-token SID. For each prefix g from first three codes only, M_g=sum_{i:c123_i=g} sum_j A_ij*1[c12_j!=c12_i]. For paired occupied siblings g,h with same c12, add relu(m+M_g-M_h)^2 whenever M_g>M_h; this is a balance hinge, not an average over level 4. Rank each g by outgoing successor count, assign extension rank blocks of 32; no prefix operation sees fourth tokens.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs: train sequences, item embeddings, RQ-VAE codebooks, minibatch transitions, k, gamma, tau, Sinkhorn iteration count, margin m, and extension block K=32. Outputs: updated codebooks/encoder, item SIDs [N,4], sparse A and s tensors, and metrics (ER, survival, T3/T4 accuracy). make_train_behavior(train_split) must also support checker-provided actual, mean, and zero signals.

specification.text: make_train_behavior(train_split) returns s_i=log(1+incoming train transition count) and a sparse directed transition matrix A_ij (counts, row normalized). At each minibatch, form Lorentz points u_i=exp_o^k(z3_i), codewords v_c, C_ic=d_L,k(u_i,v_c)^2. Set row mass r_i=(1+gamma*s_i)/sum_i(1+gamma*s_i), column capacity h_c=1/256. Compute entropy-regularized Sinkhorn T=argmin_{T>=0} <T,C>+tau sum T(log T-1), T1=r, T^T1=h; use T as soft assignment for level-3 commitment/reconstruction gradients and hard argmax_c T_ic for emitted codes. For each three-code prefix g=(c1,c2,c3), define successor mass M_g=sum_{i in g} sum_j A_ij * 1[j's first-two prefix differs from g's first-two prefix]. For sibling prefixes sharing first two codes, train Lbal=sum_(g,h) relu(m+M_g-M_h)^2 for ordered pairs where M_g> M_h; compute only g,h from levels 1-3. After training, within each g rank items by (-log(1+sum_j A_ij), item_id) and allocate fixed 32-item extension slots.

ideas.title: Successor-balanced geodesic residual transport for three-token prefixes

per_scorer_objection.scoring_1: The behavior statistic is only standardized log outdegree, not successor-community choice: items with the same outdegree receive the same b_i, and the code-specific learned h_k can reduce the behavior effect to arbitrary code bias. The tail rank then sorts by essentially the same popularity statistic, without establishing that popularity is recommendation-relevant conditional on the three-code prefix.
per_scorer_objection.scoring_2: The stated b_i is standardized log outdegree, not the successor-popularity statistic used for post-fit sorting; this does not establish that the assignment bias identifies successor communities, while the measured entropy stratification concerns a different signal.
per_scorer_objection.scoring_3: The scalar is standardized log outdegree, not a successor-community or successor-choice statistic; it cannot distinguish items with equal outdegree but entirely different successor distributions, weakening the stated continuation rationale.

per_scorer_rationale.scoring_1: E5 provides measured, covered entropy/top-successor stratification, supporting a plausible behavior problem (4), although it does not directly validate outdegree as the needed branch signal. The coupling changes curved assignment, but no cancellation or matched-control argument establishes a uniquely geometric contribution (3). E16 is unchecked literature and the proposal resembles measured successor-geodesic/tangent-residual families in E6/E7, so novelty is only a routine variation (2). The proposed assignment and ranked extension give a specific route to T3/T4 and recommendation (4). No explicit three-arm matched protocol/failure criterion (2). Cost claims are detailed, but straight-through gradients through argmin and the stated balance loss are not sufficiently specified to reproduce reliably (2). Similarity to measured behavior/geometry mechanisms limits exploration value (2). UNKNOWN: whether outdegree ordering adds conditional predictive value; resolve with a train-only conditional successor-prediction probe within fixed (z1,z2,z3) groups.
per_scorer_rationale.scoring_2: E5 supports heterogeneous successor predictability but does not measure this outdegree signal's coverage or relation to SID assignments, so behavior is plausible/testable, not well-supported for this mechanism. The Poincare distance plus additive learned code bias is curved computation, but a matched Euclidean distance with the same bias could reproduce the conditioning (E15 only says a control is proposed); no necessity argument or cancellation analysis is given. Novelty is low-to-moderate because E16 is NOT_CHECKED and E6 already measures nearby successor-geodesic and tangent-residual families. The assignment-to-prefix-to-next-item chain is plausible, but collision sorting and balance hinge have unverified utility. Counts use stop-gradient and straight-through logits without a defined estimator/gradient or a complete three-arm control protocol; the detailed cost estimate does not resolve numerical or affordability risks.
